subject: history_social
passage: In April 1815, Mount Tambora, a volcano on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa, erupted with enormous force, sending vast amounts of ash and gas high into the atmosphere. The following year, people in Europe and North America lived through a strangely cold summer: frosts damaged crops in New England in June, and harvests failed in parts of Europe. At the time, few people suspected that the two events were linked. Only in the twentieth century did scientists show that particles from large eruptions can spread around the globe and block some sunlight, cooling distant regions.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: A cold summer far from Tambora was likely caused by its eruption, a link recognized only later.
choices.B: The eruption of Mount Tambora caused frosts and crop failures across Indonesia in 1816.
choices.C: People in 1816 quickly realized that a distant volcanic eruption had cooled their summer.
choices.D: Frosts damaged crops in New England during June of the year after Tambora erupted.

explanation.why: The text pairs two events, the 1815 eruption and the cold summer that followed in Europe and North America, and then explains that the link between them was not understood until the twentieth century, when scientists showed how eruption particles can cool distant regions. The main idea combines the connection with the late recognition of it.
explanation.A: Correct. This joins the text's two parts: the eruption probably caused the distant cold summer, and scientists made the connection much later.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes cold and crop failures in Europe and North America, not in Indonesia.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says that at the time "few people suspected that the two events were linked."
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is one example of the cold summer; it leaves out the eruption's role and the later scientific explanation.
